Effects on the blood. Abnormalities in platelet aggregation were associated with fluoxetine given to a severely underweight patient.1 Platelet activity returned to normal when fluoxetine was stopped. Fluoxetine was also suspected of being the cause of bruising in a patient whose blood clotting parameters were with- in normal limits.2 Purpura and bruising have been reported to be the commonest adverse blood effects associated with fluoxetine, paroxetine, or sertraline although cases of thrombocytopenia have been recorded for all three antidepressants.3 The suggested mechanism was inhibition of uptake of serotonin into platelets, thereby disrupting platelet aggregation; caution was recom- mended when treating patients with a history of bleeding disor- ders with SSRIs.
